links.outcome: Geometric and dosimetric performance change after software upgrade of DLS model versus prior version
links.effect: Head and neck, thorax and male pelvis showed overall consistent performance after 2024A upgrade; version differences limited to selected structures (p<0.05), plus one true spinal canal segmentation failure found only on case-level review.
links.quote: However, in one patient, the 2024A model failed to correctly segment the spinal canal and instead generated a contour along the chest wall.

links.outcome: Local performance of DLS versus clinical reference contours, with decision on commissioning by site
links.effect: Abdomen commissioned (DSC 0.95 ± 0.014); breast model not recommended for clinical use (DSC 0.66 ± 0.15, HD95 22.2 ± 9.6 mm) against local reference.
links.quote: Breast segmentation results showed low performance (DSC 0.66 ± 0.15, MSD 4.8 ± 1.93 mm, and HD95 22.2 ± 9.6 mm) compared to clinical reference, so the breast structure models are not recommended for clinical use.

links.outcome: Generalization of vendor DLS model to institutional contouring conventions and anatomy
links.effect: Breast model discrepancy attributed to differences in contouring guidelines and styles between training data and institutional data; prostate spacers degraded accuracy; unusual anatomy not evaluated.
links.quote: The breast DLS model was evaluated in version 11B but was not commissioned for clinical use at that time because of the large discrepancy between DLS and the clinical segmentations, likely due to differences in contouring guidelines and styles between the model training data and the institutional contour data.

links.outcome: Revalidation of model after software update to detect performance changes
links.effect: Regression testing after 2024A upgrade found selective version differences (e.g., mandible, lungs, esophagus, prostate improved; spinal cord DSC decreased significantly p<0.001 due to one failure case).
links.quote: Version‐related differences were selective rather than consistent across sites.

links.outcome: Pre-release testing of updated model for errors using prior commissioning datasets
links.effect: Regression testing of upgraded model detected a true spinal canal segmentation failure and a breast segmentation of the shoulder, plus significant changes for several structures.
links.quote: This represented a true segmentation failure and highlights the importance of case‐level review following model updates.

links.outcome: Unsafe or inaccurate DLS outputs at case level reaching users
links.effect: Isolated failures found: spinal canal contour along chest wall in one thorax patient, shoulder segmented as breast in one case; esophagus truncated with dose errors up to ~46%.
links.quote: In one right‐sided breast case, the model incorrectly segmented a shoulder as Breast_R target volume, showing the low robustness performance of the DLS model.

links.outcome: Performance variation across anatomic sites and structures
links.effect: DSC varied by site: breast 0.66 vs abdomen 0.95; small structures such as cochleae and optic nerves had lower DSC (0.65–0.75).
links.quote: Geometric agreement varied primarily with structure characteristics rather than disease site.

models_evaluated: RayStation DLS U-Net model version 2024A SP3 (software build 15.1.3.10)

links.outcome: Post-upgrade segmentation performance
links.effect: After upgrade, head/neck, thorax, male pelvis had mean DSC 0.81±0.09, 0.84±0.13, 0.89±0.06; selected paired differences p<0.05.
links.quote: Regression testing showed that, in comparison with the previously commissioned data, mean [± standard deviation (SD)] DSC values were 0.81 ± 0.09 for the head and neck, 0.84 ± 0.13 for the thorax, and 0.89 ± 0.06 for male pelvis.

links.outcome: Local regression testing after software upgrade
links.effect: Regression testing found consistent performance for commissioned sites, abdominal model commissioned, breast not recommended; selected structures changed significantly (p<0.05).
links.quote: Regression testing of head and neck, thorax, and male pelvis sites showed consistent performance after the software upgrade and the DLS models for abdominal site were commissioned in this study for clinical use; while the DLS models for breast site were not recommended.

links.outcome: Local commissioning decision
links.effect: Local clinical-reference testing found breast low performance: DSC 0.66±0.15, MSD 4.8±1.93 mm, HD95 22.2±9.6 mm; not recommended.
links.quote: Breast segmentation results showed low performance (DSC 0.66 ± 0.15, MSD 4.8 ± 1.93 mm, and HD95 22.2 ± 9.6 mm) compared to clinical reference, so the breast structure models are not recommended for clinical use.

links.outcome: Local contouring-practice shift
links.effect: Breast DLS was not commissioned because of large DLS-clinical discrepancies attributed to training versus institutional contouring guideline/style differences.
links.quote: The breast DLS model was evaluated in version 11B but was not commissioned for clinical use at that time because of the large discrepancy between DLS and the clinical segmentations, likely due to differences in contouring guidelines and styles between the model training data and the institutional contour data.

links.outcome: Unrepresented prostate spacer anatomy
links.effect: Prostate spacer cases (SpaceOAR, Barrigel) had accuracy suffering because altered anatomy was not represented in training data; no spacer-specific metrics reported.
links.quote: Version 2024A improved somewhat over 11B, but accuracy still suffered with prostate spacing agents (SpaceOAR, Barrigel), since these alter local anatomy in ways not represented in the DLS training data.

links.outcome: Case-level segmentation failure
links.effect: One 2024A case failed spinal canal segmentation, placing the contour along the chest wall.
links.quote: However, in one patient, the 2024A model failed to correctly segment the spinal canal and instead generated a contour along the chest wall.

links.outcome: Auto-segmentation geometric performance across software versions
links.effect: Lung_R DSC improved significantly (p = 0.04), whereas Lung_L DSC decreased significantly (p = 0.03) and MSD worsened (p = 0.02), while most other structures were consistent across versions.
links.quote: In the thorax cohort, significant improvement was observed for Lung_R DSC ( p = 0.04), whereas Lung_L showed a significant decrease in DSC ( p = 0.03) and worse MSD ( p = 0.02).
